title: RAW INCOMPLETE: lexical noun phrases and finite verbs repeat an explicitly bound number feature
summary: An invented small language writes ordinary lexical words in subject-object-verb order. Eight taught endings mark subject/object case or assertion/directive mood together with singular/plural. Each noun phrase writes its kind word and full referent name; adjectives agree with that phrase, while the distant finite verb agrees only with the written subject. Open terminology requires its ordinary spelling and an explicitly known lexical sense and valency, not a hidden whole-clause code. This constructs a source-side realization of the older agreement idea, not a new discovery of agreement. Its twenty-two-working-sign carrier and historical-content compilation remain unpaid. No native values, counts or statistical success are claimed.

design.mechanism: Write separate lexical noun, adjective and verb words. Mark their grammatical roles with a small inflection table. Reuse one explicitly supplied grammatical number feature at the subject head, its modifiers and its finite verb, even when a complete differently numbered object phrase intervenes. No previous-sentence topic, hidden paragraph state, nearest-ending partner search or repeated plant identity is used.
design.unit: An ordered text of ground factual clauses and directives over named nonempty participant sets, optionally combined into explicit conditionals and postchecked until-loops. A noun phrase supplies a kind, a literal referent-set name, singular/plural and an ordered list of positive or negative properties. A verb has a known lexical sense and one or two ordered participants.
design.contrast: Unlike951, one written lexical word does not contain an entire logical statement and there are no four universal property roots. Unlike the fixed942 tuple pair, agreement repeats a grammatical feature rather than the subject's identity in a second content tuple. Unlike B6 systems2/6, the additional obligation is typed agreement at independently determined phrase positions, including an object-number countercase; this is not just a larger replacement for their old root table.
design.prediction: Changing only subject number changes the subject head, every subject modifier and the finite verb. Changing only the object number changes the object phrase but never the finite verb. Substituting another same-number subject kind or referent name does not by itself change the verb's agreement ending. These are exact consequences of this invented grammar, not native observations.
design.scope: Complete abstract teaching grammar on the stated finite-lexicon input domain. Incomplete as a physical22-sign script or general historical-language translator. The syntactic lesson is preserved RAW for manual review only.

input_domain_and_meaning.named_sets: Each noun phrase names a particular nonempty participant set with a fully written nonempty literal label. SG means exactly one member; PL means at least two and gives no exact count. A label identifies a participant set, not a whole message. If the input specifies an exact count, individual member list, measurement or unit beyond this distinction, the present language cannot silently discard it; that input is outside the contract.
input_domain_and_meaning.why_names_are_mandatory_here: This deliberately narrow lesson uses separately named sets so that reference is explicit before agreement is read. A normal language can certainly say the water or the leaves without an added proper name. Requiring a name at every NP is therefore a costly design restriction, not a linguistic necessity or a claim about historical recipes. It may make the writer impractically formulaic. Names are not made optional after that objection; an ordinary definite/indefinite reference grammar would be another declared contract.
input_domain_and_meaning.noun_kinds: A noun states the kind of each member of its named set. The learner knows the kind and its count unit. For a material, the count unit must be declared, for example a separately designated mixture batch; a mass is not silently converted to portions. Names need not describe their members or encode their number.
input_domain_and_meaning.properties: Every adjective gives one independently understood unary property of the named set's members, distributively. Positive and negative occurrences are retained in source order. Repeating an adjective repeats that property occurrence; it does not automatically mean greater degree, plurality or repeated action.
input_domain_and_meaning.verbs: Each lexical verb entry declares arity and the interpretation of singular/plural participant sets. This prevents an unspoken choice between one collective action and an action for every pair of members. A technical predicate not understood by the reader needs an explicit learned definition; full spelling alone does not teach its meaning.
input_domain_and_meaning.statements: A factual clause preserves its named participants and nominal descriptors together with the positive or negated lexical relation. A directive commands or prohibits the lexical action on those same explicitly described participants. Negating a factual relation is not prohibiting an action. Nominal descriptions remain in the recovered clause and are not silently turned into new state changes.
input_domain_and_meaning.conditions: A condition is a complete factual clause. Its truth requires its stated participant-kind/property conditions and its positive or negative predicate. IF performs its command block once only when that condition holds. REPEAT performs its command block once before testing its UNTIL condition, then repeats while false. A source requiring zero iterations or a different scope is not equivalent input.
input_domain_and_meaning.unsupported: No unresolved pronoun, implicit participant, quantifier alternation, exact numeral/unit, tense, passive voice, comparative degree, arbitrary three-place verb, indefinite-reference introduction or hidden speaker address is supplied. Such content needs a separately declared extension or must be rejected. Imperatives still write their subject; YOU is not silently inserted. This grammar is not claimed to cover all of b6.7 or b6.8.
input_domain_and_meaning.normalization: The writer receives declared content and lexical senses, not a raw historical sentence whose interpretation has somehow been solved. Original spelling and synonym choice need not be reconstructed, but every distinction admitted to this content domain is retained. Historical ambiguous alternatives must be settled or retained outside this proposed compiler before use.

lexical_learning.rule: A public lesson lexicon L lists each ordinary spelled citation, its word class, one lexical sense, and, for verbs, its valency and set interpretation; for nouns it lists the count unit. No citation denotes an entire sentence. Within one class a citation cannot covertly select between two meanings or valencies. An explicitly spelled disambiguated citation and another paid entry are required for such a second sense.
lexical_learning.open_words: The language can use any additional ordinary term once its complete citation and required lexical information are supplied to both writer and reader. There is no new arbitrary short cipher root per concept. The full ordinary spelling is written every time. This is a vocabulary-learning or dictionary-lookup cost, not a free universal primitive. Proper referent names need no concept-root entry but are always fully written; knowing the name alone does not reveal the named set's members.
lexical_learning.frozen_trial_requirement: For any future source trial, L and the ordinary-language senses used by that trial must be fixed and fully listed beforehand. Unknown content cannot be rescued after an outcome by calling it one new compact word. An incomplete L does not justify deleting an input concept.

teaching_lexicon.sense: cold; an ordinary qualitative thermal description, no hidden numerical threshold
hot; an ordinary qualitative thermal description, not simply the logical negation of cold
the subject participant or participants act jointly to heat all members of the object set
teaching_lexicon.set_interpretation: one collective operation on the whole named object set, not one separately counted operation per subject-object pair

teaching_lexicon.sense: the subject participant or participants act jointly to stir all members of the object set
teaching_lexicon.set_interpretation: one collective operation on the whole named object set; no number of turns is encoded

teaching_lexicon.sense: every member of the subject set is boiling
teaching_lexicon.set_interpretation: distributive state predicate; only factual mood is licensed for this lesson entry

teaching_lexicon.sense: every member of the subject set is flowing
teaching_lexicon.set_interpretation: distributive state predicate; only factual mood is licensed for this lesson entry

lexical_learning.not_a_large_dictionary_claim: The twelve teaching entries support the examples, not every recipe concept or arbitrary source. A practical full language can require hundreds or thousands of learned entries. Neither that ordinary lexical burden nor an additional physical character table is claimed free. The historical Lingua-ignota note motivates taking real vocabulary costs seriously; it supplies none of these invented words or grammatical rules.

teaching_orthography.warning: The following Latin-letter roots, endings, punctuation and uppercase control words are explanatory writing, not values assigned to any Voynich signs or words. They are not a frozen22-sign carrier. In particular, no native r/l/k/t value or agreement family is asserted.
teaching_orthography.root_spelling: An unquoted citation consists of one or more lowercase a-z letters. Any citation containing another allowed character is enclosed in double quotes. Inside quotes a literal double quote is backslash-double-quote; nothing else is an escape. Backslash is not admitted as literal input. Quotes preserve the entire citation, including spaces, case, hyphens and punctuation; they do not turn an unknown clause into one lexical term.
teaching_orthography.literal_domain: The same83-character content inventory used by951: a-z, A-Z, äöüßÄÖÜẞ, digits0-9, . , ; : ! ? ( ) - / ' and double quote, plus space. Any unsupported character is an explicit input stop. The Roman teaching backslash and angle/square brackets are control notation whose physical cost still needs a22-sign realization.
teaching_orthography.inflection_boundary: Append one hyphen and exactly one ending after the complete unquoted or quoted lexical citation. A negative property or verb has the control prefix non- before that citation. A source citation containing its own hyphen is quoted, so the prefix and suffix remain unambiguous. Noun heads cannot take the non- prefix under this lesson.

eight_endings.na: subject nominal or its modifier, singular
eight_endings.ne: subject nominal or its modifier, plural
eight_endings.ta: object nominal or its modifier, singular
eight_endings.te: object nominal or its modifier, plural

teaching_orthography.names: Immediately after every noun head write one separate name token <"full label">. Its full literal string is required even when the same name appeared earlier. No short register index or implicit name carry exists. Spaces inside its quotes are literal label content, not phrase boundaries. A future physical writer must pay their encoding; the teaching display does not establish a one-native-word name token for free.
teaching_orthography.punctuation: An ordinary teaching space separates tokens outside quotes. A period closes each simple clause. IF, THEN, REPEAT and UNTIL are four reserved whole control tokens. Square brackets delimit their complete scopes. All these visible marks are paid notation; none can disappear from a future carrier without a complete replacement rule.

exact_grammar.subject_phrase: One N-class head ending na or ne; its mandatory full name token; then zero or more J-class modifiers with exactly the same na/ne ending. Each modifier may have its own non- prefix. A new nominal head of the same case cannot silently begin another participant phrase.
exact_grammar.object_phrase: One N-class head ending ta or te; its mandatory full name token; then zero or more J-class modifiers with exactly the same ta/te ending. Subject and object cases are disjoint and independently supplied; matching number does not merge their referents.
exact_grammar.simple_clause: One complete subject phrase, then exactly one complete object phrase iff the final verb has lexical class V2, then one finite V1/V2 word and period. V1 permits no object phrase. The finite verb carries the subject's number and its factual or directive mood. Its number never comes from the closest modifier or from the object. The verb entry must license that mood. No other words may intervene or remain unparsed.
exact_grammar.simple_fact: A simple clause ending in mo or mi, optionally prefixed non- on its verb. The non- here negates the stated relation only; it does not negate the nominal descriptors or assert a different property.
exact_grammar.simple_command: A simple clause ending in ko or ki, optionally prefixed non- on its verb. Positive directs the named subject set to perform the action; non- prohibits that action. The same prefix on an adjective instead means that adjective is false of its own named participant set, not that an action is prohibited.
exact_grammar.command_statement: A simple command, IF [ one simple fact ] THEN [ one nonempty command block ], or REPEAT [ one nonempty command block ] UNTIL [ one simple fact ]. A command block is an ordered sequence of command statements. Nested brackets fix scope; there is no unstated ELSE.
exact_grammar.text: An ordered sequence of simple facts and command statements. Brackets and finite clauses must close completely. Paragraphs and physical line wraps merely separate whitespace outside quotes; they never create/reset a topic, change agreement or resolve a name. A physical22-sign long-word continuation convention is not provided by this abstract lesson.
exact_grammar.uniqueness: At clause start read one noun head and its required name. Following adjective words belong to that phrase only while their case/number matches. An object head begins the separate object phrase. A finite ending closes the clause's word sequence; its lexical entry fixes arity and its written number must equal the subject head. This is a deterministic typed parse of the teaching tokens. Search over matching endings is not part of reading.
exact_grammar.repetition: Repeated modifiers remain separate ordered occurrences and may be adjacent identical words. Repeated clauses or commands are written in full; there is no obligatory single REPEAT abbreviation. The reserved REPEAT control expresses the supplied until-loop only. A doubled substring inside one lexical stem is not automatically reduplication, plurality or iteration; it needs a legitimate lexical/word-formation account.

write: Take a covered interpreted clause. Write the subject kind word with na/ne from its supplied number, followed by the entire subject name. Write its supplied modifiers in order with that same subject ending.
If the verb is V2, write the complete object phrase with its own ta/te, full name and modifiers. Do not use its number to choose the verb ending.

Write the full ordinary verb citation with factual mo/mi or directive ko/ki, taking number from the subject. Add non- only at the exact supplied negative adjective or negative factual/prohibited verbal node. Close the clause with a period.

For supplied conditional or until control, write the reserved control words and all scope brackets around the complete clauses/blocks. Repeat full referent names inside each clause. No prior topic or paragraph reset is consulted.

Reject an unsupported lexical sense, valency, exact quantity, unresolved pronoun or missing participant. Learning or defining an additional ordinary word is an explicit lexical expansion, not a silent new compact code.
read: Read quoted citations and name strings literally. Segment the explicit suffixes and non- prefixes outside quotes.
Build the one subject phrase and optional object phrase in the fixed order, retaining kinds, names, number and each modifier. Validate modifier agreement and verb arity.
Check the finite verb against the subject's number, even across the object phrase. Reject a mismatch; do not search for a more convenient agreeing noun.

Use mood and prefix position to recover assertion, denial, directive, prohibition or a negative nominal property. Follow the visible brackets for IF and the postchecked until-loop, preserving command order.
Return the complete named-participant clause/control structures. Do not resolve names to an illustration, infer missing group members or claim a recovered historical spelling.

hand_worked_examples.reading: The one worker in the set named Nara, described as cold, heats the one vessel in the set named Vela, described as clean.
hand_worked_examples.trace: worker-na fixes subject singular and cold-na modifies exactly that subject. vessel-ta opens a distinct singular object phrase and clean-ta modifies exactly that object. The final heat-mo is factual singular because its subject is Nara. Vela does not become a topic for any later clause.

hand_worked_examples.reading: The multiple workers in the set named Nara, each described as cold, jointly heat the one clean vessel named Vela.
hand_worked_examples.contrast: Against base, this independent counterfactual message changes only the supplied cardinality feature of the named subject set. na becomes ne at head and modifier, and distant mo becomes mi at the verb. The intervening object words remain unchanged. The label itself contains no number code; no exact plural count is claimed.

hand_worked_examples.reading: The one cold cook named Mira heats the one clean vessel named Vela.
hand_worked_examples.contrast: Subject lexical kind and literal identity differ from base, but both are singular. The agreement ending remains mo. Replacing only Nara by Mira while retaining worker-na would likewise not change the ending.

hand_worked_examples.reading: The one cold worker named Nara heats all the clean vessels in the plural object set named Vela.
hand_worked_examples.contrast: Only object number changes. Its head and modifier take te, but the distant finite verb remains mo. Writing heat-mi would be invalid: the closer plural object is not the agreement controller. No nearest-match selection is allowed.

readings: The singular worker heats the singular vessel described as not hot; not-hot is not silently replaced by cold.
The singular worker does not heat the singular vessel: a negative factual relation.
The singular worker is forbidden to heat the singular vessel: a directive, not the negative factual assertion.

hand_worked_examples.text: REPEAT [ worker-na <"Nara"> mixture-ta <"Luma"> stir-ko . ] UNTIL [ mixture-na <"Luma"> boil-mo . ]
hand_worked_examples.reading: Have the one named worker Nara stir the one named mixture batch Luma once; then check whether Luma is boiling, repeating that instruction while it is not. Luma is the command's written object and the condition's separately written subject.
hand_worked_examples.scope_check: The repeated full name supplies the cross-clause identity explicitly. Neither positional carry nor agreement equates two otherwise different names. The first stirring is compulsory even if boiling held initially; a zero-iteration instruction is outside this particular construction.

hand_worked_examples.reading: The subject descriptor contains two cold-property occurrences in sequence, followed by the same heating assertion. Their repeated truth condition is redundant, not a claim of extra coldness or two workers. Other adjectives can repeat by the same rule, with their own full spellings.
hand_worked_examples.limit: This permits whole-word doublets without one mandatory repeat header. It does not establish the native ol/olol relation or guarantee a useful reason for every redundant source description.

costs_and_open_debt.learning: Eight inflectional forms; the subject-object-verb and modifier placement rules; the agreement-controller rule; one negative prefix with its typed scope; quotation/names/punctuation; four control words with explicit bracketing and loop timing. Every lexical citation additionally needs its sense/class and relevant count-unit, valency and collective/distributive interpretation. The twelve supplied entries are only a lesson, not a compressed universal vocabulary.
costs_and_open_debt.memory: During a clause, retain its subject number until the finite verb, the current noun-phrase case/number while reading its modifiers, and whether an object phrase has occurred. Nesting needs a visible-scope stack. Referent identity does not persist implicitly: full names are written in every clause. The reader can look back in the sentence; long clauses impose a real lookup burden.
costs_and_open_debt.written_redundancy: Agreement deliberately repeats information. Every noun head and adjective carries its case/number ending; every finite verb carries subject number and mood. Full names and full open lexemes are not abbreviated. All brackets, control words, quotes and clause boundaries are paid. No savings, plausible native mean length or low frequent-word concentration is claimed.
costs_and_open_debt.carrier: There is no complete22-working-sign representation of these citations, endings, names, punctuation or overwide words. The Roman endings are not native suffix values. A future carrier must pay every literal character, marker, exception and continuation before experimental selection. No old B6/951 glyph table is silently reused, and no whole quoted name is charged as one free native glyph or native word.
costs_and_open_debt.source_compilation: Assigning participant sets, case, lexical senses and scope to an actual historical text is a separate accountable interpretation. This artificial language does not settle b6.7's open pronouns, comparisons or vecht/veist/abe readings and does not claim b6.8 coverage. No new source or target text was encoded.

design.smallest_decision_changing_check: Before any corpus work or carrier fitting, give a table-only reader the fixed lesson and the base/subject-number/object-number/identity-change examples in an order chosen by root. Require recovery of the explicitly selected subject, independent object, number and verbal mood, without searching for matching endings or consulting a hidden source tree. The central adversarial case has singular subject and plural intervening object: a reader or implemented rule that chooses plural verb agreement from that object fails this contract. This would test this teaching language's paid distinction only; a successful hand reading is not statistical fit or native agreement. A physical-shape test still requires a frozen paid carrier, and no such test is selected by this RAW card.
design.next_physical_question_not_selected: A concrete small realization family would replace the eight taught inflections by eight fixed, distinct terminal working signs, with a separately paid lexical stem channel. In that family a noun and each of its modifiers must have exactly the same terminal sign; a singular/plural subject ending determines one of two declared verb-ending pairs according to factual/directive mood, independently of the object ending. Every two-sign inflected word would require a one-sign lexical stem; long fully spelled citations cannot be called such stems for free. These are necessary character consequences of that prospective family, not consequences of every possible carrier. Names, controls, stem/sign collisions and continuation are still unpaid, so this family is not a selected complete writer or a native agreement test. A literal non-erasing spelling of the displayed two-letter endings would already force every nonempty inflected lexical word to be at least three working signs; it should not be launched as if its ordinary content words could explain native two-sign groups. No suffix glyphs or root codes are assigned here and no repair series is authorized by this note.
known_countercases_and_limits: IP021's all-partner equality count collapses to per-line inventories; no such native count is proposed. The controller here is independently fixed by the declared subject-case grammar and named source input, not by a matching ending or nearest compatible word.

IDEA077 already states selected-versus-unselected participant-number sensitivity. The present work is a concrete invented source grammar and hand lesson for that old principle, not a new empirical discovery or reopening of its missing native observation.

A language in which a verb agrees with its object, shows semantic rather than grammatical agreement, permits number-neutral verbs, or changes agreement under coordination is a different contract. No exception can be added retrospectively when the present rule meets a contrary example.

Plural morphology does not itself decide collective versus distributive meaning. Each predicate's set interpretation is explicitly learned here; the source-review distinction retained in IDEA866 remains necessary.

Existing whole-word repetitions and diverse endings are not enough. This abstract language supplies no proof that a physical carrier can express the known short whole forms, their five-sign union, or a whole B and BB. Those obligations must be checked before a substantial source encoding, without inventing a new lexical entry for a target word.

The invariant whole-word alias bounds concern their specified inputs/groupings. This language cannot claim to pass them merely by changing its input to preinterpreted content. Any new source account must preserve all its declared distinctions and be fixed before outcomes.

Learned vocabulary can be large, but unlisted meanings and arbitrary whole-clause labels remain prohibited. The difference between a real ordinary-language lexical resource and a per-target free table is substantive, not cured by calling either one a lexicon.

predecessors.relation: Lexical heads, bound grammatical material, paid mood and valency are already present. Their fixed three-sign table and the later29-root parser/cost stops remain closed. New work here is specifically distributed case/number agreement with an independently fixed controller, not a relabeled table or a claim that those systems lacked meaning.

The strongest relevant design restriction: an all-partner ending count identifies inventory composition, not selected nonlocal grammar. Its actual negative alternatives are retained; no new native survey is proposed.

Closest semantic hypothesis: selected-set number changes a form, unselected-set changes do not. It lacks an owned native contrast; this invented lesson does not supply one or restart the flower-count route.

Scope, participant state and collective meaning cannot be read from dual morphology alone. All sixteen frozen1105 candidates were later contradicted. No historical thermal/noun values, owner rule or source restriction is imported here.

Shared material/action stems and valency were already proposed conditionally on an independently frozen channel. This lesson introduces no automatic noun-to-verb conversion and no abbreviation decoder.

This is not a larger951 root inventory, a repaired947 iteration parser or a renamed B6 carrier. It has separate lexical phrase words and repeatedly explicit participant names; the old conditional physical exclusions remain unchanged.
A real learned lexicon with bounded shared pieces and irregular wholes motivates honest vocabulary costs. It does not attest this invented SOV grammar or link it to Voynich.
